title: Anatomy of a Paradigm Shift: How the Transformer Architecture Redefined Natural Language Processing
hook: By eliminating recurrence in favor of pure self-attention, the Transformer architecture shattered the sequential bottleneck of RNNs and fundamentally altered the trajectory of representation learning.

sections.heading: The Sequential Bottleneck of Recurrent Models
key_points: Inherent sequential dependency of RNNs, LSTMs, and GRUs prevents parallelization across time steps during training.
Vanishing and exploding gradient pathologies over long contexts degrade the modeling of long-range dependencies.
Hidden state compression forces all historical context into a fixed-size vector, creating an information bottleneck.

sections.heading: Mechanics of Scalable Self-Attention
key_points: Scaled dot-product attention computes interactions between all token pairs simultaneously with $O(N^2)$ time complexity.
Query, Key, and Value projections allow the model to dynamically weight token relevance regardless of positional distance.
Multi-head attention projects representations into different subspace representation spaces to capture diverse syntactic and semantic relationships.

sections.heading: Positional Encodings and Permutation Invariance
key_points: Self-attention operations are permutation invariant, treating inputs as sets rather than ordered sequences.
Sinusoidal and learned absolute positional encodings inject token order information into the initial embedding layer.
Modern relative positional biases and rotary embeddings (RoPE) improve extrapolation to longer sequence lengths during inference.

sections.heading: Foundation Models and Downstream Transfer Learning
key_points: Task-agnostic pre-training objectives like masked language modeling and causal autoregression extract rich contextual features.
Scale laws demonstrate predictable improvements in loss as a function of compute, parameter count, and dataset size.
In-context learning and parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) enable rapid adaptation without architectural modifications.

conclusion_point: The Transformer's decoupling of sequence length from sequential computation unlocked unprecedented scale, transforming NLP from task-specific feature engineering to universal representation learning.
topic: Why the Transformer architecture changed NLP
